title: Joshua Tree · Full-Moon Scramble Weekend — February 2027

packing: Scramble kit: grippy approach shoes, flexible pants, tape and small first-aid kit; Joshua Tree granite is abrasive.
Winter desert layers: puffy, shell, warm hat and gloves for freezing/windy dawn and night sessions.
Photo kit: tripod, intervalometer, fast wide lens, telephoto and spare batteries kept warm.
Car kit: offline NPS map, water for everyone, headlamps and a full fuel tank before entering.

itinerary.labelHtml:
Day by Day

Four nights from one Joshua Tree cabin

Each day shows the actual driving load, a sunset or night-light plan, food fallbacks and a safe exit.

days.heading: Pittsburgh → Palm Springs → Joshua Tree
days.feel: Land, stock the cabin, catch first sunset
days.daycost: Est. $520 · flight share, car, groceries and dinner
days.note: Pick up the rental, stop at Vons in Yucca Valley before checking in, then use Cap Rock only if the daylight margin is comfortable. Sunset is about 5:34 p.m.; no racing.

spots.climate: Cool, sunny days can flip to freezing, windy evenings. Granite is especially slick when wet; skip all squeezing and scrambling after rain.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk the official one-mile Hidden Valley loop and let the kids choose only obvious, reversible boulder moves beside the trail.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Book a five-hour private family climbing session; the current Cliffhanger four-person rate is $125 each.

spots.climate: Feb 20 is a full moon, not a dark-sky Milky Way night. Use moonlight as a giant softbox for trees and boulders; the galactic core is below the horizon in February.
spots.saveHtml: Save Walk Mane Street, eat early and photograph moonlit Joshua trees from a legal paved pullout.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge A fast prime lens and sturdy tripod matter more than an expensive workshop on these bright nights.

spots.cost: Optional guided half-day: currently $500 total for four with Cliffhanger Guides. Park pass is separate. Reserve only after confirming minimum ages, footwear and cancellation terms.
spots.climate: Dry rock is the gate. A guide can choose age-appropriate top-rope terrain and adjust for wind; do not substitute unguided technical climbing.
spots.saveHtml: Save Skip ropes and combine Barker Dam with supervised ground-level boulder play.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge The guide is the trip’s best paid upgrade: real helmets, ropes and instruction rather than improvising on abrasive granite.

days.feel: A scenic-drive day with small scrambles
days.note: Start at Twin Tanks for Arch Rock, picnic at Skull Rock/Jumbo Rocks, then reach Cholla well before the 5:36 p.m. sunset. Leave before the road feels tiring in darkness.

spots.cost: All stops are covered by the park pass. Arch Rock is now a 1.4-mile route from Twin Tanks; White Tank is not the public trailhead.
spots.climate: Start early and carry layers. The Cholla Garden has almost no shade, and detached cactus joints can puncture shoes and skin—stay on the path and never touch.
spots.saveHtml: Save Pack lunch and use the free roadside hikes and overlooks.
spots.splurgeHtml: Splurge Spend on the climbing guide, not another tour; this scenic drive is strongest self-guided.
spots.restoHtml:
• Kitchen in the Desert — stylish Twentynine Palms dinner; verify kid fit and hours
  • Jelly Donut — simple breakfast stop in Twentynine Palms
  • Crossroads Cafe — burgers, breakfast and sandwiches
  • Joshua Tree Saloon — burgers, fries and a broad menu
  • Vons Yucca Valley — full grocery and familiar-food fallback
spots.altboxHtml:
• Split Rock Loop replaces Cholla if the east-side drive feels long.
  • Oasis of Mara is a very short accessible walk near town.

February avoids heat and wildfire season, but winter storms can bring freezing nights and occasional snow.

Four family hikes, one optional squeeze

Distances are official where a trail exists. Hall of Horrors is deliberately treated as unsignposted scrambling, not a guaranteed route.

Turnaround rule: if a child cannot reverse a move without a boost, it is not casual scrambling. No jumping down, no climbing over rock art, and no slots after rain.
